B1.question: How does RAG combine parametric and non-parametric memory?
B1.answer: RAG combines parametric and non-parametric memory by using a pre-trained seq2seq transformer (BART) as parametric memory and a dense vector index of Wikipedia accessed by a pre-trained neural retriever (DPR) as non-parametric memory. These components are combined in a probabilistic model trained end-to-end: the retriever provides latent documents conditioned on the input, and the seq2seq model conditions on these latent documents together with the input to generate the output. Latent documents are marginalized with a top-K approximation, either per-output (same document for all tokens) or per-token (different documents for different tokens). (Retrieval-Augmented Generation | rag_paper.pdf)

B1.question: What are the two RAG model variants proposed in the paper and how do they differ?
B1.answer: The two variants are RAG-Sequence and RAG-Token. RAG-Sequence uses the same retrieved document to generate each target token, treating the document as a single latent variable marginalized over top-K documents. RAG-Token can predict each target token based on a different document, allowing the generator to choose content from several documents when producing an answer. (Retrieval-Augmented Generation | rag_paper.pdf)

rows.question: How does RAG combine parametric and non-parametric memory?
rows.answer: RAG combines parametric and non-parametric memory by using a pre-trained seq2seq transformer (BART) as parametric memory and a dense vector index of Wikipedia accessed with a pre-trained neural retriever (DPR) as non-parametric memory. These components are combined in a probabilistic model trained end-to-end, where the retriever provides latent documents conditioned on the input, and the seq2seq model conditions on these latent documents together with the input to generate the output. Latent documents are marginalized with a top-K approximation, either per-output (same document responsible for all tokens) or per-token (different documents responsible for different tokens). (Retrieval-Augmented Generation | rag_paper.pdf)

rows.question: How does RAG combine parametric and non-parametric memory?
rows.answer: RAG combines parametric and non-parametric memory by using a pre-trained seq2seq model (BART) as parametric memory and a dense vector index of Wikipedia accessed with a pre-trained neural retriever (DPR) as non-parametric memory. These components are combined in a probabilistic model trained end-to-end: the retriever provides latent documents conditioned on the input, and the seq2seq model conditions on these latent documents together with the input to generate the output. Latent documents are marginalized with a top-K approximation, either on a per-output basis (same document for all tokens) or per-token basis (different documents for different tokens). Both the generator and retriever are jointly learned during fine-tuning. ("Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks")

rows.question: How does RAG combine parametric and non-parametric memory?
rows.answer: RAG combines parametric and non-parametric memory by using a pre-trained seq2seq transformer (BART) as parametric memory and a dense vector index of Wikipedia accessed with a pre-trained neural retriever (DPR) as non-parametric memory. These components are combined in a probabilistic model trained end-to-end, where the retriever provides latent documents conditioned on the input, and the seq2seq model conditions on these latent documents together with the input to generate the output. The latent documents are marginalized with a top-K approximation, either on a per-output basis (same document responsible for all tokens) or per-token basis (different documents responsible for different tokens). (Retrieval-Augmented Generation | rag_paper.pdf)

rows.question: What is the purpose of the scaling factor sqrt(dk) in Scaled Dot-Product Attention?
rows.answer:
The scaling factor √dk counteracts the effect of large dot products pushing the softmax function into regions with extremely small gradients. For large values of dk, dot products grow large in magnitude, which can cause vanishing gradients; scaling by √dk mitigates this issue.

rows.question: How does RAG combine parametric and non-parametric memory?
rows.answer: RAG combines parametric and non-parametric memory by using a pre-trained seq2seq transformer (parametric memory) and a dense vector index of Wikipedia accessed with a pre-trained neural retriever (non-parametric memory). These components are combined in a probabilistic model trained end-to-end. The retriever provides latent documents conditioned on the input, and the seq2seq model conditions on these latent documents together with the input to generate the output. Latent documents are marginalized with a top-K approximation, either on a per-output basis (same document responsible for all tokens) or per-token basis (different documents responsible for different tokens). ("Retrieval-Augmented Generation | rag_paper.pdf")

rows.question: How does RAG combine parametric and non-parametric memory?
rows.answer: RAG combines parametric and non-parametric memory by using a pre-trained seq2seq transformer as parametric memory and a dense vector index of Wikipedia as non-parametric memory, accessed with a pre-trained neural retriever. The retriever provides latent documents conditioned on the input, and the seq2seq model conditions on these latent documents together with the input to generate the output. The latent documents are marginalized with a top-K approximation, either on a per-output basis (same document responsible for all tokens) or per-token basis (different documents responsible for different tokens). The components are combined in a probabilistic model trained end-to-end. (Retrieval-Augmented Generation | rag_paper.pdf)

rows.question: What are the two RAG model variants proposed in the paper and how do they differ?
rows.answer: The two RAG model variants are **RAG-Sequence** and **RAG-Token**. They differ in how they handle retrieved documents during generation: RAG-Sequence uses the **same retrieved document to predict each target token** (treating the document as a single latent variable marginalized over the whole sequence), whereas RAG-Token can **predict each target token based on a different document** (drawing a different latent document for each target token and marginalizing accordingly), allowing the generator to choose content from several documents when producing an answer. [Retrieval-Augmented Generation | rag_paper.pdf]

rows.question: How does RAG combine parametric and non-parametric memory?
rows.answer: RAG combines parametric and non-parametric memory by using a pre-trained seq2seq transformer as parametric memory and a dense vector index of Wikipedia as non-parametric memory, accessed via a pre-trained neural retriever (DPR). These components are combined in a probabilistic model trained end-to-end, where the retriever provides latent documents conditioned on the input, and the seq2seq model conditions on these latent documents together with the input to generate the output. Latent documents are marginalized with a top-K approximation, either per-output (same document responsible for all tokens) or per-token (different documents responsible for different tokens). (Retrieval-Augmented Generation | rag_paper.pdf)

rows.question: How does RAG combine parametric and non-parametric memory?
rows.answer: RAG combines parametric and non-parametric memory by using a pre-trained seq2seq transformer (BART) as parametric memory and a dense vector index of Wikipedia accessed with a pre-trained neural retriever (DPR) as non-parametric memory. These components are combined in a probabilistic model trained end-to-end: the retriever provides latent documents conditioned on the input, and the seq2seq model conditions on these latent documents together with the input to generate the output. Latent documents are marginalized with a top-K approximation, either on a per-output basis (same document responsible for all tokens) or a per-token basis (different documents responsible for different tokens). (Retrieval-Augmented Generation | rag_paper.pdf)

rows.question: How does RAG combine parametric and non-parametric memory?
rows.answer: RAG combines parametric and non-parametric memory by using a pre-trained seq2seq transformer (BART) as parametric memory and a dense vector index of Wikipedia accessed with a pre-trained neural retriever (DPR) as non-parametric memory. These components are combined in a probabilistic model trained end-to-end, where the retriever provides latent documents conditioned on the input, and the seq2seq model conditions on these latent documents together with the input to generate the output. Latent documents are marginalized with a top-K approximation, either on a per-output basis (same document responsible for all tokens) or per-token basis (different documents responsible for different tokens). [Retrieval-Augmented Generation | rag_paper.pdf]

rows.question: What are the two RAG model variants proposed in the paper and how do they differ?
rows.answer: The two RAG model variants are **RAG-Sequence** and **RAG-Token**. They differ in how they handle retrieved documents during generation: RAG-Sequence uses the same retrieved document to predict each target token in the sequence, while RAG-Token can predict each target token based on a different document, allowing the generator to choose content from several documents when producing an answer. english.question: What are the two RAG model variants proposed in the paper and how do they differ?
english.answer: The two variants are RAG-Sequence and RAG-Token. RAG-Sequence uses the same retrieved document to generate each target token, treating the document as a single latent variable marginalized over top-K documents. RAG-Token can predict each target token based on a different document, allowing the generator to choose content from several documents when producing an answer. (Retrieval-Augmented Generation | rag_paper.pdf)

B5.question: Both papers use a Transformer-based sequence-to-sequence generator. What does Attention remove from its architecture, and what external memory does RAG add to its generator?
B5.ground_truth: Attention removes recurrence and convolutions, relying on attention. RAG uses BART-large as its seq2seq generator and augments it with a dense vector index of Wikipedia passages accessed by a retriever.
B5.section: Attention Abstract/§3; RAG §2.2 Retriever: DPR y §2.3 Generator: BART
B5.answer: Attention removes recurrence from its architecture. RAG adds a dense vector index of Wikipedia, accessed with a pre-trained neural retriever (Dense Passage Retriever), as external memory to its generator. (rag_paper.pdf)
